To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the power optimization of data dominated multimedia applications is orthogonal to the performance improvement by the exploitation of sub word parallelism, and (ii) the application of our transformations is typically more beneficial than the exploitation of sub -word parallelism for the complete application, and it enhances the effect of the latter.

(a) the application of our power optimizing code transformations is orthogonal to the subword parallelisms exploitation and (b) that the performance improvement of the application of our code transformations is larger than the performance improvement due to subword parallelism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an application mapping methodology that allows to achieve the best possible trade-off between the performance and power consumption of applications mapped on the target architecture.
the combined application of low-power code transformations and the exploitation of sub word parallelism.
the development of a methodology to reduce the power consumption of multimedia applications on VLIW multi media processors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power optimizing code transformation approach and the exploitation of sub- word parallelism should be applied together for the mapping of multimedia applications on VLIW multimedia processors.

the application of the code transformations approach for the reduction of power consumption due to data transfers and storage has a positive impact on both power and performance of multimedia applications realized on VLIW multi- media processors.

the power optimizing code transformation methodology is a very effective approach for the reduction of power consumption of data-dominated applications realized on the VLIW multi-mediacore architecture platform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
power optimizing code transformations and the exploitation of sub word parallelism should be combined in the mapping of multimedia applications on VLIW multi media processors.
the application of power optimizing code transforms is orthogonal to the sub-word parallelism exploitation.
the exploitation of sub word parallelism should be performed after the application of power optimizing code optimizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application of the proposed transformations can be considered as an important step in the development of a methodology for the power optimization of applications realized on VLIW multimedia processors.

the application of power optimizations and performance optimizations is complementary and that the positive effects of the application of power optimizing code transformation on performance are typically larger than the negative effects of these transformations on performance.
our power optimizing code transformations can be applied in a very effective way to multimedia applications that are realized on VLIW multi- media processors.
